newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Mack-Cali tightens grip on NJ office market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mack-Cali tightens grip on NJ office market.

text.p: Cali Realty Corp can become the dominant player in commercial real estate in its own New Jersey market and develop a presence in Texas and Arizona through its prooposed $1.2 billion acquisition of two privately-held real estate companies.
Cali Realty said on Thursday it agreed to buy the office assets of Mack Co in New Jersey and Patriot American Office Group in Texas.

When the merger is completed before the end of the year, the Cranford, N.J. real estate investmet trust, will own eight percent of all office space in central and northern N.J., about 11 million square feet.
At the same time, the company, to be renamed Mack-Cali Realty Corp, said the acquisitions, will where Patriot American operates 17 offices in Dallas, Houston, San Antonio and Amarillo.
The deal is also being put together in a real estate market that has been rising.
"If I look at the real estate cycle in general, there is about four years more in the cycle, and it will last even longer with some restraint," said Bill Mack, senior managing partner of The Mack Co.
Mack owns 17 million square feet of space in and around New Jersey, about 35 percent of which is offices. "We see that we are probably in the mid-innings ogf an extra-inning game," he said.
Office REITs are one of the strongest areas in real estate, and investors looked favorably on the deal, with Cali stock trading at 37-3/4 Thursday afternoon, up 2.
Management said that deal would add $0.25 per share to funds from operations.

One of the advantages of the deal is that it leaves Cali with a relatively low level of debt, about 30 percent of its total $3.3. billion capitalization. That will give it the flexibility to make further acquisitions and to develop its own properties.
"Our debt used to be in the mid-30s, but we've brought it down and we're comfortable with that,' said Thomas Rizk, chief executive of Cali.

"I think 30 percent is in line with what you'd expect from a quality REIT. Its relatively conservative and gives them some additional flexibility," said Fred Harmeyer, an analyst at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co. "You'll see a shift of focus to new development as opposed to making acquisitions," he said.
"We are developers," said Mitchell Hersh, chief operating officer of Mack. "We've developed 10 million square feet of space in New Jersey."
